name: Venera 13
first: Longest surface survival of any Venus mission (127 min); first colour panoramic images and first audio from another planet's surface
description: The peak of the Soviet Venera program. Venera 13 launched 1981-10-30 and landed 1982-03-01 at 7.5°S 303°E in the Phoebe Regio highlands. Surface conditions at touchdown: 457 °C, 89 bar, sulfuric-acid haze. The lander survived 127 minutes — nearly an hour beyond its design target — returning the first colour panoramas from another planet's surface, recording wind microphone audio, and using its drill + onboard X-ray fluorescence spectrometer to determine that the basalt at the landing site was a weakly differentiated leucite alkaline composition. Twin spacecraft Venera 14 performed identical operations at a separate site five days later. The Venera series (1967–1983) remains the only successful surface program at Venus to date.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: Proton-K / D-1 lifts Venera 13 from Baikonur on a 122-day cruise.

events.label: VENUS SURFACE LANDING
events.note: Touchdown in Phoebe Regio at 7.5°S 303°E; 127 minutes of surface operations under 457 °C / 89 bar.
